system.name: Case to Resolution on an AI service desk (AI-SaaS example)
system.description: The same case process as the Agent-PaaS Case to Resolution example, run on a vendor's managed AI service desk. The SaaS vendor builds and runs the agents, the policy service, the runtime and the gateway, and gets the reasoning LLM from its own AI Model Provider. The customer owns the process, the hard-rule values it sets in the service, its customer data, and the business response. Under AI-SaaS the SRF matrix shows the customer's L5 cell as N/A, so the customer has no model duty of its own at L5.
system.operating_model_note: Example assumption: the customer subscribes to a managed AI service desk and configures it. Bill to confirm.

obligations.title: Protect personal information of customers and complainants
obligations.applies_if: Case or profile records hold personal data of individuals in scope. Needs counsel.

obligations.title: Verify identity, enforce refund and goodwill caps, and follow required escalation paths before closing a case
Keep each customer's case and account data confidential
Do not use unfair or deceptive acts or practices in the handling of a customer case

obligations.applies_if: The conduct is in scope of the cited law. Needs counsel.

obligations.title: Handle covered consumer complaints through the required channel and within required timeframes
obligations.applies_if: The case is a covered consumer complaint. Needs counsel.

obligations.title: Give required consumer disclosures and do not omit a fact needed to make a statement not misleading
obligations.instrument: Consumer disclosure rules applicable to the product (candidate)
obligations.applies_if: A required disclosure applies to the product or the remedy. Needs counsel.

controls.title: L1 owner approves every version of the case orchestration logic
No agent can approve its own output (segregation of duties)
Refund and goodwill caps enforced by the policy service; dual approval above the cap
Mandatory escalation categories enforced by the policy service; the agent cannot close those cases itself
Identity verification must pass, or a documented exception must be on file, before account changes
Treat customer chat and email text as data, never as instructions
Each agent has a scoped identity and least-privilege tool access
Output filtering before any customer message is sent
Regression test set run before any model, prompt or setting change; L1 owner approves results
L1 owner is named as the change approver for model settings
Log rule version, inputs, decision and authority for each step; check decisions against policy, not against the model's stated reasoning
Agent context limited to one customer and one case at a time
Dual approval for changes to customer contact and payout details
Identity scores below a confidence threshold go to a person
Covered complaints routed to the required register and clock before any close
Required disclosures inserted from the policy service, not from model text
Resolution offers checked against approved remedy matrices; no waiver of a required right

threats.title: A crafted customer message makes the intake agent open a case against the wrong account

risk.failure_mode: Untrusted message text treated as a verified claim
risk.impact: A case is opened or changed on another customer's account

threats.title: Unapproved edit to the orchestration logic skips identity verification

risk.failure_mode: Step order changed without L1 approval
risk.impact: Account changes proceed without a verified identity

threats.title: Reasoning LLM reads 'make this right for a loyal customer' as permission to exceed the refund cap

risk.failure_mode: A service slogan is read as a waiver of a hard rule
risk.impact: A remedy is issued above approved authority

threats.catalog_note: No entry in /data/threats.json matches this threat. The catalog's model-behavior entries, such as evasion and prompt injection, assume an attacker. Here the model misreads plain business wording and no attacker is involved, so the threat is left unmapped.
threats.notes: Accountable: the AI Model Provider on the provider side (Bill, Nov 17, 2026). Under AI-SaaS the customer's L5 cell is N/A: the customer cannot test or pin the model. The customer's levers are the hard-rule values in the policy service, the L1 business response, and change-notice terms in the SaaS contract.

threats.title: Gateway falls back to a smaller model under load and triage or remedy decisions change

risk.failure_mode: Fallback model used without an L1-approved change
risk.impact: Cases are classified or resolved differently than under the pinned model

threats.title: Orchestrator chains steps so an investigation note is treated as a remedy approval

risk.failure_mode: A recommendation is treated as an approval
risk.impact: A refund or goodwill credit is issued without the required authority

threats.title: A customer argues the resolution agent into a refund above the approved cap

risk.failure_mode: Agent accepts a verbal workaround as authority
risk.impact: A remedy is issued above approved authority

threats.title: Investigation agent puts one customer's case data in another customer's reply

risk.impact: Another customer's case data is disclosed

threats.title: Customer payout details changed in the profile to divert a refund

risk.failure_mode: Payout details changed without dual approval

threats.title: Guardrail service is down and agents run without output filtering

risk.failure_mode: Agents continue when filters are unavailable
risk.impact: Unfiltered customer messages leave the system

threats.title: Identity component marks a session as verified when the feed would not have supported it

risk.failure_mode: Score does not reflect the feed
risk.impact: Account changes proceed on an unverified identity

threats.title: Orchestrator closes a covered consumer complaint before the required channel and clock are met

risk.failure_mode: Mandatory escalation skipped or run late
risk.impact: A covered complaint is closed without the required handling

threats.title: Resolution agent offers a remedy and omits a required consumer disclosure

risk.failure_mode: Disclosure text comes from model language, or is omitted
risk.impact: The customer does not receive a required disclosure
